execution_steps: 1. Checked git log/status for concurrent-worker conflicts -- clean, no new commits since this session's own Event 335 commit.
2. Re-read components.py's own current implementation (replace_party) and module docstring in full before designing anything new, to confirm the exact pattern being generalized.

3. Read the pinned UBL 2.3 Invoice maindoc XSD directly (src/python/ubl/src/format_factory/ubl/validation/schemas/maindoc/UBL-Invoice-2.3.xsd) rather than assuming cardinality from memory -- grepped for PaymentMeans/TaxTotal/AllowanceCharge and confirmed all three declare maxOccurs='unbounded', minOccurs='0', directly inside the root Invoice element's own top-level sequence (same indentation/context as the already-handled AccountingSupplierParty).

Recognized the key generalization: Party's own single-occurrence property made 'find the one existing wrapper' trivial, but for a REPEATING component, Update (replacing an ALREADY-PRESENT occurrence by its own existing index) is STILL simple -- it's Create (adding an ADDITIONAL occurrence) that needs the arbitrary-position insertion logic replace_party's own docstring correctly identified as out of scope. This is a different axis than single-vs-multi-occurrence: it's about update-vs-create regardless of cardinality.
